classification.difficultyReason: Identify opposite sides, apply the cosine rule to find angles including an obtuse angle, and use the angle sum.

content.prompt: $AB=8$ cm, $BC=6$ cm and $AC=12$ cm. Find the magnitude of each of the angles of triangle $ABC$ correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Unmarked scalene triangle with A lower left, B above A and left of C, and C at the right. Only vertex labels are printed. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Triangle ABC; AB=8 cm, BC=6 cm and AC=12 cm are supplied in the prompt. Diagram is schematic, with no added measurements or angle marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex labels and triangle remain visible; no answers are shown.

answer.short:
$A=26.4^\circ$, $B=117.3^\circ$, $C=36.3^\circ$.

Use the cosine rule, then the angle sum of a triangle.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\cos A&=\frac{8^2+12^2-6^2}{2\times8\times12}\\
\cos A&=\frac{43}{48}\\
A&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{43}{48}\right)\\
A&\approx26.4^\circ\\
\cos B&=\frac{8^2+6^2-12^2}{2\times8\times6}\\
\cos B&=-\frac{11}{24}\\
B&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(-\frac{11}{24}\right)\\
B&\approx117.3^\circ\\
C&=180^\circ-\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{43}{48}\right)-\cos^{-1}\!\left(-\frac{11}{24}\right)\\
C&\approx36.3^\circ
\end{align*}$$
The angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$. All angles are rounded to one decimal place.
